expectations.text: Identifies the dead admin-fallback bug (onlyRole(ISSUER_ROLE) blocking the documented '(or admin)' fallback) in at least one of registerPlots/issue/reissue/revoke
expectations.evidence: Finding #1 (rated High), same mechanism correctly named across all four functions, with the same doc-comment quoting and same root-cause explanation as the with-skill run.

expectations.text: Identifies the reassignBeneficiary + reissue() manufactured-beneficiary combo as a critical unilateral theft path an issuer can execute against their own issued certificates
expectations.evidence: Finding #2 discusses reassignBeneficiary and cancelReissueProposal but frames the risk purely as 'a REVOKED issuer retains stale power' -- it explicitly says the blast radius is 'limited because reissue() itself is correctly gated,' missing that a CURRENT, non-revoked issuer can call reassignBeneficiary then immediately reissue(INHERITANCE) to bypass admin confirmation entirely. The actual critical bug (manufactured consent, no revocation required) is never stated.

expectations.text: States a concrete exploit call sequence (specific function calls in order, not just 'this could allow theft')
expectations.evidence: No numbered call sequence for any finding; findings are described conceptually with code snippets and prose ('if admin.revokeRole... is called... badIssuer can still...') rather than a step-by-step reproducible sequence, and nothing was executed against compiled bytecode.

expectations.text: Assigns differentiated severity -- treats the manufactured-beneficiary bug as materially more severe than the dead-admin-fallback bug, rather than flat-listing all findings at the same weight
expectations.evidence: Top severity used is 'High' for the dead-admin-fallback finding; the actually-critical manufactured-beneficiary bypass was never identified as its own finding, so no Critical tier appears anywhere despite a Critical-grade bug existing in the contract.

expectations.text: Delivers corrected code (not prose-only description) if the user's framing ('I'm building') suggests they'd want a fix
expectations.evidence: Each finding includes a Solidity fix suggestion (e.g. re-checking hasRole(ISSUER_ROLE,...) in reassignBeneficiary/cancelReissueProposal), though none were compiled or test-verified.
